title:
Private Deployments 

VPC & On-Prem Reference: Deployment, Day-2 Ops, Upgrade & Rollback, and Customer Requirements
author: Ethan Chen
body:
Overview

This page is a consolidated reference for Redwood Inference private deployments (VPC and on-prem). It covers: reference architectures, pre-deployment requirements, packaging and installation patterns, day-2 operations, and tested upgrade & rollback procedures. Intended audience: SREs, Platform Engineers, Solutions Engineers, and Customer Success engineers supporting private customers.

Scope
- Applies to both VPC-backed private deployments (cloud-managed control plane with customer VPC peering/privatelink) and fully on-prem (air-gapped) installations.
- Excludes hosted API operation and Redwood Dedicated public-cloud managed capacity.

Key contacts and ownership
- Product/Program owner: Ethan Chen (eng)
- Primary oncall for private deployments: eng-private-deployments oncall rotation
- Escalation: Lead: Priya Nair; Backup: Miguel Alvarez

Reference architectures (summary)
1) VPC Deployment (recommended for most enterprise customers)
   - Components: Control plane (Redwood-managed) + Customer VPC for data plane (K8s cluster, GPU nodes).
   - Network: VPC peering or PrivateLink; strict egress controls; NAT for outbound updates optional.
   - Storage: NFS/CSI-backed block store for model artifacts and caching; S3-compatible object store for long-term artifacts.
   - Identity: Customer-managed IAM + OIDC for node identity; KMS integration for keys.
   - Sizing: 1 coordinator (m5/4vcpu) + GPU pools sized to model throughput (e.g., p4d / a100 nodes).

2) On-Prem / Air-Gapped Deployment
   - Components packaged as airgap bundle (images + manifests + offline installer).
   - Network: No outbound internet; internal registry required.
   - Storage: SAN/NAS for persistent PVs; local NVMe for KV/prefix caches recommended.
   - Security: HSM/KMS integration optional via customer network paths; offline license key validation flow provided.

Pre-deployment checklist (customer requirements library)
- Network & Routing:
  - CIDR ranges allocated for control and data plane.
  - Ports open between control plane IPs and worker clusters: 443 (API), 9000-9100 (internal services) - confirm with solutions engineer.
  - PrivateLink or VPN established for VPC mode.
- IAM & Identity:
  - OIDC provider configured for Kubernetes (issuer URL).
  - Service accounts, RBAC roles defined per install manifest.
- Storage:
  - Object store endpoint (S3-compatible) with credentials and bucket names.
  - Persistent volumes class and reclaim policy for model store and logs.
- Compute & GPUs:
  - GPU node type and counts; driver versions (CUDA) compatible with chosen model runtime.
  - Node labels for scheduling (e.g., gpu-type: a100).
- Secrets & Keys:
  - KMS/HSM connection details or vault path for encryption keys.
  - TLS certificates for control plane and ingress (or use Redwood-provided if VPC).
- Compliance & Data Residency:
  - Data flows documented; any cross-region replication approved.

Packaging & installation patterns
- VPC mode (managed control plane):
  1. Customer provides cluster kubeconfig and private endpoints.
  2. Redwood installer (helm chart + operator) applied via secure channel.
  3. Operator registers nodes and configures model pool.
  - Typical install command (example):
    kubectl apply -f redwood-operator-v1.4.0.yaml --context=\"<customer-cluster>\"
    helm repo add redwood https://charts.redwood.ai/stable
    helm upgrade --install redwood-platform redwood/redwood-platform -n redwood --values customer-values.yaml

- On-prem airgap:
  1. Provide airgap bundle (images.tar.gz) and offline installer tarball.
  2. Customer loads images into local registry:
    docker load -i images.tar.gz && docker push <local-registry>/redwood:v1.4.0
  3. Apply manifests that reference local-registry images and local object store endpoints.

Common configuration snippets
- Example customer-values.yaml (key entries):
  controlPlane.endpoint: \"https://control.redwood.example\"
  registry.endpoint: \"registry.local:5000\"
  storage.s3.endpoint: \"https://s3.internal.example\"
  runtime.gpu.nodeSelector: \"gpu-type: a100\"
  security.kms.path: \"/vault/data/redwood/keys\"

Day-2 operations (runbook highlights)
- Monitoring & Observability:
  - Metrics to surface: per-model QPS, token latency (p50/p95/p99), KV cache hit rate, GPU utilization, OOM events.
  - Dashboards: per-cluster model performance, per-route latency breakdown, cost-per-token analytics (console integration).
  - Alerts (recommended thresholds):
    - Token latency p95 > 2500ms for 5m -> P1 (pager)
    - GPU utilization > 85% sustained for 15m -> P2
    - Model OOM rate > 1% -> P2
- Backups & Artifact Management:
  - Model store snapshots daily; retention 14 days by default.
  - Critical config (RBAC, secrets) exported to secure store continuously.
- Scaling & Capacity:
  - Autoscaling: horizontal pod autoscaler for stateless API, cluster autoscaler for GPU nodes.
  - Recommended burst capacity: +20% GPU buffer for onboarding new models.
- Regular maintenance:
  - Weekly: dependency patching scan.
  - Monthly: run smoke tests against canary model to detect regressions.

Upgrade & rollback procedures (tested pattern)
- Principles:
  - Prefer canary-first with traffic shifting.
  - Maintain backwards-compatible model and runtime schema during migrations.
  - Keep db migrations reversible or zero-downtime where possible.

- Pre-upgrade checklist:
  1. Verify healthy cluster: no node pressure, all pods Ready.
  2. Run preflight (redwoodctl diagnose --cluster <ctx>).
  3. Ensure backup of model store and etcd/metadata (snapshot).
  4. Notify stakeholders and schedule maintenance window if required.

- Canary upgrade steps (example using helm/operator)
  1. Push new images to registry and update Chart version.
  2. Deploy canary subset: set replica count for api gateway to 1 and route 5% traffic to canary via traffic manager.
    - helm upgrade redwood-platform redwood/redwood-platform --set canary.enabled=true --set canary.percent=5
  3. Monitor for 30-60 minutes; check error rates, latency, and model correctness evals.
  4. If stable, increase canary percent incrementally to 100% and remove old release.

- Rollback plan (if canary fails)
  - Immediate action: route 100% traffic back to previous release via traffic manager and scale down canary.
  - Command example:
    trafficctl set-weight redwood-api --revision previous --weight 100
    helm rollback redwood-platform <previous-release-revision>
  - Postmortem: capture logs, collect traces, and file incident report with root cause analysis.

- Forced rollback (on-prem offline)
  - Restore from model store snapshot and redeploy the previously validated airgap bundle.
  - Validate with smoke tests before restoring traffic.

Testing & validation (post-upgrade smoke tests)
- Smoke test suite includes:
  - API health endpoints
  - Latency regression test (compare to baseline)
  - Deterministic prompt-eval against golden prompt set (pass/fail thresholds)
  - End-to-end end-user flow for critical routes

Operational playbook snippets
- Incident triage (fast path):
  1. Pager triggers -> acknowledge and claim.
  2. Run triage checklist: check control plane connectivity, cluster node status, and etcd health.
  3. If GPU nodes down: check driver & kernel versions, restart kubelet on affected nodes.
  4. If model corruption: restore model artifact from snapshot.

SLOs, SLIs and alerting thresholds (recommended)
- API availability: 99.95% monthly
- Token latency: p95 <= 2500ms for standard models (customer SLA adjustable)
- Error rate: 0.5% for 5-minute window (P1 if > 1%)

Appendix: Customer Requirements matrix (example table)
| Requirement area | Must-have | Recommended | Notes |
|------------------|-----------:|------------|-------|
| Network          | VPC CIDR, PrivateLink/VPN | NAT for outbound updates | Provide test connectivity file (iperf) |
| Identity         | OIDC issuer, service accounts | RBAC review checklist | Attach example RBAC YAML |
| Storage          | Object store endpoint, PV class | Local NVMe for cache | Include credentials vault path |
| Compute          | GPU type, driver version | Node labelling for pools | Provide sample TF module for node pool |
| Security         | TLS certs, KMS path | HSM integration | Offline key exchange process for on-prem |
